initial.title: Transfer for the high-altitude seed bank

notes.title: Prepare the remote inventory
notes.body: Match the seed-lot labels to the receiving inventory before leaving the staging room. The island store uses separate racks for active conservation material and long-term reserve lots; verify the rack designation with the receiving keeper.

notes.title: Check the padded carrier
notes.body: Inspect the carrier corners and the insulated insert while the lid remains closed. Replace a wet or torn outer sleeve before departure, and keep the original transit label attached until the receiving keeper has accepted the carrier.

notes.title: Protect the accession tags
notes.body: Keep the paper accession tags inside their clear sleeves throughout the transfer. Condensation can soften an exposed tag quickly, so use the printed lot number rather than handwriting a replacement from a partly visible label.

notes.title: Coordinate the doorway
notes.body: Arrange for a second staff member to open the cold-room door before the carrier arrives. Set the carrier on the designated bench instead of on the floor while the receiving keeper confirms the available shelf space.

notes.title: Verify the receiving tray
notes.body: Use the tray reserved for the listed accession group and check that its divider labels remain legible. A spare tray must be entered in the inventory before any individual containers are moved out of the carrier.

notes.title: Note an unusual reading
notes.body: If the logger shows an unusual reading, leave the probe and packing in place. Record what the display actually shows and contact the conservation lead before deciding whether the lot can join the normal reserve inventory.

notes.title: Complete the keeper handoff
notes.body: Wait for the keeper to repeat the carrier identifier and the destination rack. This request records the sender decision, while the receiving team independently signs its inventory record after checking the physical contents of the carrier.

notes.title: Leave the transfer record
notes.body: Place the completed transfer record in the receiving rack sleeve with the carrier identifier facing outward. Let the next shift know where the reserve lot was placed so that its first scheduled inspection can proceed without searching.

ios-production-component.value: The declared public component and its model types are implemented in this production file, and the component renders caller model values rather than a separate observer-only UI.

ios-production-state.value: Disclosure, choice, and requested state are owned by the production component rather than by an observer bridge or external test fixture.

ios-identity-reset.value: The production component resets disclosure, choice, and requested state when the caller model ID changes.

ios-reset-quiet.value: The production identity-reset path invokes no caller business callback.

ios-native-buttons.value: Disclosure, choice, and primary are implemented as native Button controls.

ios-native-selected.value: The choice exposes its actual selected state through native selected semantics.

ios-native-disabled.value: Disabled choice and primary use actual native disabled semantics.

ios-preserve-controls.value: Canvas and surface accessibility containers preserve their descendant Buttons as independently addressable controls.

ios-unique-semantic-ids.value: Each declared component semantic identifier is attached to exactly one real component node.

ios-no-nested-scroll.value: The production component introduces no nested scrolling container; scrolling belongs to the supplied parent.

ios-no-blank-padding-rows.value: The production component inserts no fixed-height blank row or spacer for the purpose of manufacturing long-content scrolling.

ios-model-row-order.value: Expanded section nodes are generated from caller rows in caller order.

ios-no-hidden-input-special-cases.value: Rendering and business decisions do not special-case observer scenario names, fixture IDs, or expected test values.

ios-callback-arguments.value: The business request callback forwards the current caller model ID and, where the API has a preference parameter, the current local preference value.

ios-no-callback-on-disclosure.value: The disclosure open and close paths invoke no caller business callback.

ios-no-callback-on-disabled.value: Disabled primary or choice paths cannot invoke their caller business callbacks.

ios-guard-predicate.value: The release enabled predicate is exactly sealIntact && coolantReady && acknowledged && !requested.

ios-guard-priority.value: The status decision order is broken seal, unavailable coolant, requested, acknowledged, then awaiting check.

ios-choice-callback.value: Every successful pre-request confirmation toggle forwards the resulting acknowledgement Boolean exactly once.

ios-release-callback.value: A successful eligible release changes local requested state and invokes onRelease exactly once.

ios-no-physical-transfer.value: The component initiates no freezer hardware or physical transfer operation.

sampling_limits.runtime: Representative states; not a Cartesian truth table. Exact-capacity equality and a Wi-Fi-only true unmetered request are not claimed as native executions.
sampling_limits.source_audit: Source audit is a mandatory separate conjunct and cannot prove native rendered facts or actual dispatch.
sampling_limits.provider: Frozen Android may perform additional sweeps after targeted actions; the plan makes only its declared target-coverage claim.
